papers.title: Quality of postoperative recovery in patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal cancer resection as affected by transversus abdominis plane block combined with moderate neuromuscular blockade: a randomized controlled trial
papers.authors: Wang S, Xu W, Guo D, Liu C, Zhu Y, Wang X
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative recovery quality in laparoscopic surgery may benefit from deep neuromuscular blockade, whereas the effects of combining transversus abdominis plane block (TAPB) with moderate neuromuscular blockade in this regard remain unreported. This work investigated whether moderate neuromuscular blockade differs from deep neuromuscular blockade in terms of postoperative recovery quality in patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery with routine TAPB, to provide evidence-based support for optimizing perioperative neuromuscular blockade strategies.
METHODS: 110 patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery were randomized to moderate (train-of-four count 1-2) or deep (post-tetanic count 1-2) neuromuscular block, with both groups undergoing TAPB. The primary outcome was recovery quality assessed by the Quality of Recovery-40 (QoR-40) on postoperative day 1 (POD1).
RESULTS: No statistically significant between-group differences in mean POD1 QoR-40 scores were found (172.18 ± 6.78 vs. 172.51 ± 6.89; 95% CI - 2.91 to 2.26; P = 0.802), with no significant differences across the scale's five subdomains.
CONCLUSIONS: During TAPB application for laparoscopic colorectal cancer resection, no clinically meaningful differences in postoperative recovery quality were identified between moderate and deep neuromuscular blockade.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500103278, registered 27 May 2025.

papers.title: Prophylactic mesh versus no mesh for the prevention of parastomal hernia after permanent colostomy: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
papers.journal_full: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland
papers.abstract:
AIM: Prophylactic mesh at permanent colostomy formation is intended to prevent parastomal hernia, but randomised trials conflict and existing meta-analyses predate the latest long-term trial data.
METHOD: MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL were searched from inception to July 2026 for randomised trials comparing prophylactic mesh with no mesh at elective permanent colostomy formation. The primary outcome was parastomal hernia. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2; outcomes were pooled with a random-effects model (restricted maximum likelihood, Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment), and certainty was rated with GRADE (PROSPERO CRD420261442749).
RESULTS: Thirteen trials (1340 patients) were included. Mesh was associated with lower odds of parastomal hernia (odds ratio 0.38, 95% CI 0.20-0.71; I2 = 67%), but the 95% prediction interval crossed unity (0.07-2.20), and in an exploratory analysis of the six large multicentre trials, the association was attenuated and not significant (odds ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.50-1.26). Reoperation (odds ratio 0.82, 95% CI 0.53-1.27), surgical-site infection, stoma-related morbidity and mortality did not differ. Funnel-plot asymmetry was compatible with small-study effects; no trial was at low risk of bias, and certainty was low.
CONCLUSION: Prophylactic mesh may be associated with fewer parastomal hernias, but the certainty of evidence is low, and the association was weaker in large multicentre trials. Mesh may result in little or no difference in reoperation; the evidence on symptomatic hernia is very uncertain, and safety data are insufficient. Consistent with current risk-stratified guidance, mesh may be considered selectively rather than routinely.

papers.title: Salvage surgery after total neoadjuvant therapy and watch-and-wait in rectal cancer: a systematic review and proposed minimum outcome set
papers.authors: Burke J, Samuel I, Clifford R, Sutton P, Arthur C, Renehan A
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Salvage surgery for local regrowth following watch-and-wait (W&W) after total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) is perceived to be technically more difficult than immediate surgery after treatment. However, surgical difficulty lacks standardised definition and reporting. This methodological review proposes a structured minimum outcome set (MOS) to distinguish intra-operative technical complexity from surgery-related morbidity and evaluates current reporting against this framework.
METHODS: A predefined framework comprised two domains: (1) surgery-related morbidity (Clavien-Dindo major complications, 30- or 90-day mortality, anastomotic leak, reoperation/readmission within 30 days and stoma status) and (2) intra-operative technical complexity (surgical approach, conversion, operative time, blood loss and a predefined pelvic complexity metric). R0/R1 resection status was recorded separately as a contextual oncological measure. A systematic review identified studies reporting salvage surgery for local regrowth after TNT and W&W. Reporting of MOS variables was enumerated and risk of bias assessed using a topic-specific ROBINS-I tool.
RESULTS: Ten studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising 569 patients managed with TNT and W&W; 198 (35%) developed local regrowth and 172 (87%) underwent salvage surgery. Only one study reported major complications with salvage-specific denominators. Mortality, anastomotic leak, reoperation and stoma outcomes were absent or pooled. R0/R1 status was reported in seven studies but often without salvage-specific denominators. No study reported objective intra-operative metrics corresponding to predefined technical complexity variables. Risk of bias ranged from moderate to serious.
CONCLUSIONS: Current reporting is insufficient to define the safety or technical complexity of salvage surgery after TNT and W&W. The proposed MOS offers an exploratory basis for standardised reporting and may inform future consensus-driven core outcome set development.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Assessment of the Multifaceted Impact of Inflammatory Bowel Disease on Quality of Life: Insights From the IBD-PODCAST Study
papers.authors: Magro F, Dignass A, D'Amico F, Gomollón F, Dinkhauser P, Hart A
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (IBD), encompassing Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), are chronic gastrointestinal disorders, significantly affecting patients' daily lives. The "treat-to-target" approach emphasizes the enhancement of patients' quality of life (QoL) as a therapeutic target. This analysis aims to provide an overview of IBD's impact on QoL and further explore the burden related to EIMs, stool urgency, fatigue, and work productivity.
METHODS: This analysis was part of the study IBD-PODCAST descriptive cross-sectional study including 2185 CD and UC patients from 10 countries. Suboptimal disease control (SDC) based on red flags from STRIDE II recommendations was assessed. The impact of IBD on patients' QoL was assessed, and the relationships of fecal urgency, fatigue, and work productivity to QoL were examined. Comorbidities, extraintestinal manifestations (EIMs), and therapeutic approaches and their effects on QoL were also evaluated.
RESULTS: 52.2% of CD patients and 44.3% of UC patients experienced SDC. Impaired QoL was present in 70% of patients with SDC, regardless of advanced treatment use. 41.3% of CD patients and 39.4% of UC patients presented impaired QoL and 30.4% of CD patients and 27.6% of UC patients presented severely impaired QoL. Symptoms and signs of inflammation were more common among those with impaired QoL. Comorbidities (CD; 37.9% and UC; 36.1%) and EIMs (CD; 18.4% and UC; 13.5%) were linked to reduced QoL. Stool urgency was reported by 43.5% of patients, exacerbating QoL concerns. Fatigue and work productivity loss had an important impact on QoL, highlighting the significant burden of IBD.
CONCLUSION: This study underlined the multifaceted impact of IBD. It emphasizes the need for a holistic disease management approach that prioritizes not only clinical parameters but also patients' QoL, fatigue, stool urgency and work productivity. A multidisciplinary approach is crucial to provide comprehensive care for the chronic effects for patients living with IBD.

papers.title: Hemorrhoidectomy vs. non-Doppler-guided hemorrhoidal artery ligation
papers.authors: Kaya S, Tosun Y, Adıgüzel N, Altın Ö, Karahan M, Hacıalioğlu C
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hemorrhoidal disease is one of the most prevalent benign anorectal conditions, and the optimal surgical approach for higher-grade disease remains debated. Conventional excisional hemorrhoidectomy is durable but painful, whereas hemorrhoidal artery ligation with mucopexy is a minimally invasive alternative that aims to reduce morbidity. Although hemorrhoidal artery ligation was originally described as a Doppler-guided procedure, accumulating evidence has questioned whether intraoperative Doppler localization is essential, supporting fixed-position suture ligation as a simpler alternative. We compared conventional hemorrhoidectomy with non-Doppler hemorrhoidal artery ligation combined with mucopexy with respect to perioperative parameters and long-term patient-reported outcomes.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included patients who underwent conventional hemorrhoidectomy or non-Doppler hemorrhoidal artery ligation combined with mucopexy for hemorrhoidal disease between June 2023 and December 2024. The hemorrhoidal artery ligation combined with mucopexy technique consisted of a full-thickness Z-suture placed approximately 4 cm proximal to the dentate line for arterial ligation, followed by a running mucopexy of four to six mucosal-submucosal bites at 5-mm intervals down to 5 mm above the dentate line, applied to each of the three classical anatomical hemorrhoidal positions (3, 7, and 11 o'clock). Demographic and perioperative data were obtained by chart review. Postoperative outcomes were assessed by a structured telephone interview conducted blinded to the operative technique, using the Hemorrhoidal Disease Symptom Score, the Short Health Scale for Hemorrhoidal Disease, a 0-10 patient satisfaction score, the Visual Analogue Scale for pain, and the Vaizey incontinence score. Recurrence was defined as the patient's self-reported perception of a symptomatic anal lump and was not confirmed by physical examination. To account for the imbalance in hemorrhoid grade, multivariable logistic regression and a subgroup analysis restricted to grade 3 disease were performed, and effect estimates are reported with 95%CIs.
RESULTS: Of 185 patients operated during the study period, 34 were excluded, leaving 151 patients (62 hemorrhoidectomy, 89 hemorrhoidal artery ligation combined with mucopexy). The groups were comparable in sex, age, American Society of Anesthesiologists class, and smoking status (all p>0.05). Hemorrhoid grade distribution differed significantly (p<0.001), with grade 2 disease present only in the hemorrhoidectomy group. Hospital stay was shorter after hemorrhoidal artery ligation combined with mucopexy (0.8±0.4 vs. 1.1±0.6 days; p=0.001). Over a mean follow-up of approximately 29 months, postoperative bleeding, tenesmus, Visual Analogue Scale pain, Vaizey score, patient satisfaction, and Hemorrhoidal Disease Symptom Score did not differ significantly between groups. Recurrence was numerically higher after hemorrhoidal artery ligation combined with mucopexy (25.8 vs. 12.9%; OR 2.35, 95%CI 0.97-5.68) but did not reach statistical significance (p=0.083), and the study was underpowered for this endpoint (post-hoc power 51.8%). The direction of the association persisted after adjustment (aOR 2.21, 95%CI 0.91-5.38) and in the grade 3 subgroup (24.0 vs. 12.8%; OR 2.15, 95%CI 0.73-6.31). Quality of life measured by Short Health Scale for Hemorrhoidal Disease was significantly better (lower) in the hemorrhoidectomy group (6.3±4.3 vs. 8.7±3.9; p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Both techniques achieved comparable symptom control, pain, continence, and satisfaction at long-term follow-up. Non-Doppler hemorrhoidal artery ligation combined with mucopexy offered a shorter hospital stay, while hemorrhoidectomy was associated with better disease-specific quality of life and a numerically lower recurrence rate that persisted after adjustment for hemorrhoid grade but did not reach statistical significance in an underpowered comparison. The results indicate that omission of the Doppler transducer does not compromise the long-term outcomes of hemorrhoidal artery ligation with mucopexy and support an individualized approach to technique selection.

papers.title: Clinical presentation, histopathological patterns, and management approach of colorectal cancer patients at a specialized hospital in Mogadishu, Somalia: a retrospective study
papers.authors: Hassan A, Sheik A, Bashir A, Nur N, Ali A
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, with a rapidly increasing burden in sub-Saharan Africa. In Somalia, data on CRC are scarce, and patients frequently present at advanced stages. This study aimed to describe the clinical presentation, histopathological patterns, disease stage, and surgical management of colorectal cancer patients treated at a major tertiary hospital in Mogadishu.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted at Mogadishu Somali-Türkiye Recep Tayyip Erdoğan Training and Research Hospital. Medical records of all adult patients with histologically confirmed colorectal cancer who underwent surgery between January 2020 and December 2024 were reviewed. Data on demographics, clinical presentation, tumor characteristics, disease stage, surgical procedures, and postoperative complications were extracted from the hospital's electronic database and analyzed using descriptive statistics.
RESULTS: A total of 59 patients were included, of whom 69.5% were male. The mean age was 57.44 ± 16.48 years, with 32.2% of patients aged ≤ 50 years. The most common presenting symptom was intestinal obstruction (74.6%), followed by rectal bleeding (15.3%) and perforation (8.5%). The caecum (35.6%) and sigmoid colon (32.2%) were the most frequent tumor sites. Adenocarcinoma was the predominant histological type (67.8%), followed by mucinous adenocarcinoma (15.3%) and signet-ring cell carcinoma (5.1%). Well-differentiated tumors accounted for 49.2% of cases, while 30.5% were poorly differentiated. Lymphovascular invasion and perineural invasion were present in 37.3% and 42.4% of patients, respectively. Most patients presented with advanced disease, with Stage III and Stage IV accounting for the majority of cases. Surgical management was dominated by resection and anastomosis (42.4%) and end ileostomy (30.5%), with right hemicolectomy being the most common operation (42.3%). Postoperative complications included wound infection (10.2%) and anastomotic leak (8.5%).
CONCLUSION: Colorectal cancer patients in Somalia commonly present with advanced-stage disease and potentially aggressive histopathological features, leading to a high burden of emergency and palliative surgical care. Limited access to chemotherapy and the absence of radiotherapy further restrict treatment options. Strengthening early detection, diagnostic services, screening capacity, and oncology infrastructure is essential to facilitate timely diagnosis and improve colorectal cancer care in Somalia.

papers.title: Immunomodulatory and targeted therapies for metastatic colorectal cancer
papers.authors: Gao K, Lv Q, Zhao L, Wang Z
papers.abstract: Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. Its systemic treatment has evolved from conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy toward biomarker-driven targeted therapy and immunotherapy. Advances in molecular profiling have refined patient selection for anti-EGFR and anti-VEGF therapies and have enabled the development of treatments directed against BRAF V600E, KRAS G12C, HER2 amplification, and other actionable alterations. In parallel, immune checkpoint inhibitors have transformed the management of microsatellite instability-high/mismatch repair-deficient mCRC, whereas microsatellite-stable disease remains largely resistant to immunotherapy and continues to require rational combination strategies. Despite these advances, primary and acquired resistance, dynamic clonal evolution, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment remain major barriers to durable disease control. Circulating tumor DNA and multidimensional molecular profiling are increasingly being explored to monitor treatment response, identify emerging resistance, and guide sequential therapy. This review summarizes recent advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy for mCRC and discusses priorities for developing adaptive, biomarker-driven treatment strategies.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese medicine modulates immune homeostasis through the gut microbiota-microbial metabolite axis
papers.authors: Yang S, Zhang T, Guo J, Teng C, Sun W, Sun D
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota is considered a central regulator of immune homeostasis, and microbial metabolites serve as key mediators that translate microbial activity into host immune responses. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) can modulate the composition of the gut microbiota; however, changes in microbial communities alone cannot fully explain its immunomodulatory effects. Therefore, this review summarizes the mechanisms by which TCM reshapes the gut microbial metabolome and, in turn, modulates host immune responses. TCM interventions effectively promote the production of beneficial microbial metabolites, suppress potentially harmful metabolites, and enhance microbial-mediated biotransformation of phytochemicals, thereby reshaping the gut immune microenvironment. Immune signaling pathways activated by microbial metabolites include G protein-coupled receptors, aryl hydrocarbon receptors, farnesoid X receptor, Takeda G protein-coupled receptor 5, and epigenetic regulatory mechanisms; these pathways synergistically regulate mucosal immunity, immune cell differentiation, inflammatory responses, and immune homeostasis. Furthermore, this study explored the therapeutic role of the "traditional Chinese medicine-gut microbiota-microbial metabolites" axis in inflammatory bowel disease, cancer, metabolic inflammation, autoimmune diseases, and other immune-mediated conditions. This research provides a new theoretical foundation for how TCM modulates host immunity by reshaping microbial metabolites, and offers new insights for the development of interventions targeting the gut microbiota.

papers.title: Mitochondrial quality control and intestinal barrier dysfunction in inflammatory bowel disease: knowledge mapping and translational perspectives on traditional Chinese medicine-derived bioactive compounds
papers.authors: Mao Y, Zhou G, Li X, Zhang L, Wang C
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammatory bowel disease is a chronic relapsing intestinal disorder characterized by intestinal barrier dysfunction, gut microbiota dysbiosis, mitochondrial impairment, and mucosal immune imbalance. Mitochondrial quality control links epithelial energy metabolism, oxidative stress, mitophagy, inflammasome activation, and barrier homeostasis. Traditional Chinese medicine-derived bioactive compounds and natural products may provide multi-target regulatory advantages, yet the knowledge structure and translational trajectory remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to map the landscape of mitochondrial quality control and intestinal barrier dysfunction in inflammatory bowel disease and clarify the translational potential of traditional Chinese medicine-derived bioactive compounds and natural products targeting mitochondrial-related mechanisms.
METHODS: Literature was retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and PubMed from January 1, 2000 to May 31, 2026. A two-stage bibliometric and knowledge-mapping analysis was conducted. Stage 1 focused on mitochondrial quality control and intestinal barrier dysfunction, whereas Stage 2 focused on traditional Chinese medicine-derived bioactive compounds and natural products targeting mitochondrial-related mechanisms. Publication trends, countries/regions, institutions, authors, journals, keywords, and co-cited references were analyzed.
RESULTS: Stage 1 identified 909 Web of Science Core Collection records and 741 PubMed records, with publication output increasing after 2020 and reaching 198 records in 2025. This field involved 51 countries/regions, 1,128 institutions, and 5,574 authors, with the United States, China, and Germany as leading contributors. Its intellectual base centered on NOD2/CARD15, ATG16L1, autophagy, Paneth cell dysfunction, antimicrobial peptide deficiency, oxidative phosphorylation, gut microbiota, and epithelial defense. Stage 2 expanded rapidly, increasing from 32 records in 2020 to 121 in 2025. This direction involved 42 countries/regions, 592 institutions, and 2,731 authors, with China occupying a dominant position. Research hotspots shifted from pharmacodynamic evaluation and experimental colitis models toward mitophagy, oxidative stress, NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome signaling, AMPK/mTOR signaling, SIRT1 activation, gut microbiota regulation, and barrier repair.
CONCLUSION: Mitochondrial quality control is becoming a central framework for understanding inflammatory bowel disease. Current hotspots indicate a shift toward an integrated regulatory network involving mitochondria, immune responses, gut microbiota, and intestinal barrier function. Future frontiers should focus on causal validation of mitophagy-related pathways, identification of patient subgroups with abnormal mitochondrial quality control, and development of multi-target interventions to restore mucosal immune balance and barrier homeostasis. Traditional Chinese medicine-derived bioactive compounds and natural products may be valuable because their multi-pathway regulatory properties are consistent with the complex pathobiology of inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: Computed Tomographic Evaluation of Acute Colonic Disease: Current Emergency Radiology Practice
papers.authors: Hines J, Salam B, Karkala N, Doan M, Katz D
papers.abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is the primary imaging modality for evaluating acute colonic disease in the emergency setting. This article reviews CT technique, and systematically examines the imaging findings and etiologies of common colonic disease, including infectious and inflammatory colitis, large bowel obstruction, perforation, and acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding. Emphasis is placed on causes, distribution of disease, characteristic CT findings, and recognition of complications, in order to guide accurate and timely diagnosis and management.

papers.title: Impact of Climate Change on Gastrointestinal Health
papers.journal_full: Gastrointestinal endoscopy clinics of North America
papers.authors: Siau K, Thakur A, Abulhassan W
papers.abstract: Climate change is increasingly endangering gastrointestinal (GI) health. Heat stress, rising temperatures, extreme weather, humidity changes, food insecurity, air pollution, environmental contaminants, and vector-borne diseases contribute to GI disorders through mechanisms like epithelial barrier dysfunction, immune activation, and gut microbial dysbiosis. Climate-driven changes in food and water systems increase the spread of enteric infections, viral hepatitis, and parasitic diseases, while disruptions to agriculture reduce food security and nutrient availability. Air pollutants, microplastics, heavy metals, and mycotoxins further impact GI health. These exposures are linked to inflammatory bowel disease, disorders of gut-brain interaction, GI cancers, and liver disease, disproportionately affecting vulnerable populations.

papers.title: Targeting RAS Signaling Pathways: Molecular Regulation, FDA-Approved Inhibitors, Clinical Advances, and Patent Innovations
papers.authors: Chauhan A, Prajapati V, Singh A, Kalsi A, Kumar A, Mishra R
papers.abstract: RAS gene mutations play a major role in the development and progression of cancer. According to recent data, mutations in the RAS gene are responsible for nearly 30% of all cancer cases worldwide. Among these, KRAS mutations account for more than 85% of all RAS mutations and are particularly prevalent in aggressive malignancies, including colorectal cancer (CRC), non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). In this manuscript, we provide a detailed discussion of the RAS signaling cascades and their regulatory mechanisms. The catalytic region of RAS proteins, which comprises the P-loop, Switch I and Switch II regions, and RAS-effector interaction surfaces, exhibits a high degree of structural conservation across the different RAS isoforms. Sotorasib was the first covalent KRAS inhibitor to receive regulatory approval and acts by irreversibly binding to the cysteine residue at position 12 (Cys12). In this manuscript, we discuss in detail targeted RAS inhibitors, including adagrasib (MRTX849), fulzerasib (IBI351), garsorasib (D-1553), glecirasib (JAB-21822), and divarasib (GDC-6036). Finally, we focus on recent advances in RAS inhibitor patents from 2019 to the present, with particular emphasis on thiazole, benzothiazole, quinazoline, and other emerging chemical scaffolds.
